===== analysis/leg_model.py  (exit 0, 1 s)
# Leg analysis report (generated by analysis/leg_model.py)

- FK->IK round trip over joint ranges: worst error 2.61e-13 deg -> PASS
- Belt-coupling virtual-work check (tau_q = A^T tau_m, th_k = q1 + N q2): PASS

## Sanity anchors (brief 4.4, 4.5)

| knee pulley | N | max vertical F (belt 120 N, rated torque) |
|---|---|---|
| 20T | 1.0 | 8.3 N |
| 40T | 2.0 | 16.6 N |
| 48T | 2.4 | 19.9 N |
| 60T | 3.0 | 24.9 N |

Ab/ad, l=40 mm, 20 N vertical: |tau0| = 0.80 Nm; with +/-2 N lateral: 0.43 / 1.17 Nm

## Design point: L1 = L2 = 130 mm, 20T:60T (N = 3.00), l = 53.0 mm

Nominal stance height STANCE_FRAC(L1+L2) = 213 mm

- Nominal stance joint angles: q1 = -34.9 deg, q2 = 69.8 deg
- Continuous capability (+/-10% lateral, motors <= rated, belt <= 60 N): **15.4 N** vertical (target >= 15 N)
- Peak capability (motors <= peak, belt <= 120 N): **30.8 N** vertical

Static load case: 15 N down + 1.5 N lateral at nominal stance
- joint torques tau_q = [0.475, 0.000, -1.116] Nm
- motor torques [abad, hip, knee] = [0.475, 0.372, -0.372] Nm (rated 1.3)
- belt effective tension = 58.4 N (continuous limit 60 N)

## Firmware limits

- knee motor torque limit = T_peak x r_hip = 120 N x 6.37 mm = **0.76 Nm**
- hip motor: 4.1 Nm peak, set 2.5 Nm (structure SF>=2, see skeleton check); ab/ad: 2.5 Nm
- knee joint torque available at belt peak: 2.29 Nm

## Belt

- open-belt length at C = 130 mm: 341.2 mm -> 342 mm (171 teeth) + idler take-up; with 2 x 15 mm clamp overlap cut 372 mm (supplied 450 mm ASSUMED)
- preload >= 60 N per span (half of peak effective tension)
- 20T hip pulley wrap ~180 deg -> ~10 teeth in mesh; idler adds wrap

## Sweep: max continuous vertical force at nominal stance (+/-10% lateral, belt 60 N, rated torque)

| L (mm) | 40T | 48T | 60T | 48T, 24T hip (N=2) | 60T, 30T hip (N=2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 110 | 12.1 | 14.6 | 18.2 | 14.6 | 18.2 |
| 120 | 11.1 | 13.3 | 16.7 | 13.3 | 16.7 |
| 130 | 10.3 | 12.3 | 15.4 | 12.3 | 15.4 |
| 140 | 9.5 | 11.4 | 14.3 | 11.4 | 14.3 |
| 150 | 8.9 | 10.7 | 13.3 | 10.7 | 13.3 |
| 160 | 8.3 | 10.0 | 12.5 | 10.0 | 12.5 |

Belt tension depends only on the knee pulley radius; a bigger hip pulley adds teeth in mesh but lowers N.

## Ab/ad torque vs l (15 N vertical + 1.5 N lateral, nominal stance)

- l = 40 mm: |tau_abad| = 0.28 Nm
- l = 52 mm: |tau_abad| = 0.46 Nm
- l = 60 mm: |tau_abad| = 0.58 Nm
- l = 80 mm: |tau_abad| = 0.88 Nm

## Speed

- hip joint max 38.7 rad/s; knee joint (motor / N) 12.9 rad/s (rated speed)
- swing +/-60 mm in 0.2 s: I_hip ~ 22.1 kg cm^2 (extended), alpha = 55 rad/s^2, hip torque ~ 0.24 Nm
- same leg with the knee motor at the knee: I_hip ~ 53.4 kg cm^2 (2.4x)
- reflected rotor inertia: hip/abad 54 kg cm^2, knee 486 kg cm^2 (catalog 540 g cm^2 â€” if that is already output-side, divide by 100; VERIFY)




===== analysis/snow_model.py  (exit 0, 1 s)
# Snow model (analysis/snow_model.py)

Robot 4.5 kg (ASSUMED). Loads per foot: static (4 down) 11.0 N, walk (3 down) 14.7 N, trot (2 down) 22.1 N, trot peak 33.1 N.

Parameters: Lines, Elliott & Ray (2021) compiling Wong (2001); plate models for homogeneous snow — calibrate on real snow (docs/SNOW_TEST_PLAN.md) before trusting absolute numbers.

## Sanity anchors (brief 4.3)

| anchor | model | brief | |
|---|---|---|---|
| ball R10 trot pressure | 70.26 kPa | 69–71 | PASS |
| ball R10 trot foot load | 716.20 g/cm² | 710–722 | PASS |
| ball trot sinkage Bekker min | 14.61 cm | 14.5–15.5 | PASS |
| ball trot sinkage Bekker max | 29.52 cm | 29.5–30.5 | PASS |
| ball trot sinkage Preston min (P2-P5) | 19.16 cm | 18.5–19.5 | PASS |
| ball trot sinkage Preston max | 52.61 cm | 52.5–53.5 | PASS |
| snowshoe trot pressure | 2.93 kPa | 2.85–2.95 | PASS |
| snowshoe trot foot load | 29.84 g/cm² | 29.5–30.1 | PASS |
| snowshoe trot Bekker min | 5.36 cm | 5.35–5.45 | PASS |
| snowshoe trot Bekker max | 6.19 cm | 6.15–6.25 | PASS |
| snowshoe trot Preston min | 1.28 cm | 1.25–1.35 | PASS |
| snowshoe trot Preston max | 7.64 cm | 7.55–7.75 | PASS |
| snowshoe static Bekker min | 3.31 cm | 3.25–3.35 | PASS |
| snowshoe static Bekker max | 4.01 cm | 3.95–4.05 | PASS |
| snowshoe static Preston min | 0.65 cm | 0.55–0.65 | PASS |
| snowshoe static Preston max | 3.96 cm | 3.95–4.05 | PASS |
| traction snowshoe, trot, poorly bonded | 8.02 N | 7.9–8.1 | PASS |
| traction ball, trot, poorly bonded | 3.68 N | 3.6–3.8 | PASS |
| traction snowshoe, trot, well bonded | 54.61 N | 54–56 | PASS |
| compaction work per trot step, P5 | 0.82 J | 0.75–0.85 | PASS |

**Anchors: ALL PASS** (20/20)

## Foot sweep (teardrop planform, walk = snow gait load, trot for reference)

| foot L×W | area cm² | perim mm | trot g/cm² | walk sink B1–B3 cm | walk sink P4 / P5 cm | trot sink P5 cm | compaction J (walk, P5) | est. foot g | added hip inertia ×1e-3 kg m² |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100×70 | 54.5 | 274 | 41.3 | 4.8–5.8 | 4.7 / 7.1 | 10.3 | 0.51 | 28 | 1.89 |
| 110×75 | 65.1 | 300 | 34.6 | 4.3–5.2 | 4.0 / 6.0 | 8.7 | 0.43 | 30 | 2.04 |
| 120×80 | 76.5 | 325 | 29.4 | 4.0–4.8 | 3.4 / 5.2 | 7.5 | 0.37 | 32 | 2.19 |
| 130×90 | 93.4 | 357 | 24.1 | 3.7–4.3 | 2.8 / 4.3 | 6.3 | 0.31 | 36 | 2.43 |

**Chosen: 120 × 80 mm, tail radius 34** → area 76.5 cm², trot foot load 29.4 g/cm² (lynx 25.9–31.6), within the 130 × 90 limit. 100 × 70 and 110 × 75 exceed lynx-level loading in a trot; 130 × 90 sinks ~1 cm less but adds mass, inertia and clash risk between front and hind feet.

## Stepped 'hoof' pad (P2): PAD_PROUD 0 / 6 / 12 mm, walk load

| PAD_PROUD | B1 pad/deck cm | B3 pad/deck cm | P4 Lebel pad/deck cm | P5 Lebel pad/deck cm | ride height lost on rock |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 mm | 4.8 / 4.8 | 4.0 / 4.0 | 3.4 / 3.4 | 5.2 / 5.2 | +0 mm rocker under a free ankle |
| 6 mm | 5.1 / 4.5 | 4.1 / 3.5 | 3.9 / 3.3 | 5.7 / 5.1 | +6 mm rocker under a free ankle |
| 12 mm | 5.6 / 4.4 | 4.5 / 3.3 | 4.4 / 3.2 | 6.2 / 5.0 | +12 mm rocker under a free ankle |

The pad adds sinkage at the pad and gains nothing in soft snow (the deck sinks about the same). On rock or ice a proud pad makes the foot a rocker under a free-pitch ankle and lifts the spikes off the surface (spikes protrude only 3 mm). **PAD_PROUD = 0 chosen**: the pad is flush with the lug tips and acts as a solid 'hoof' zone (insert bosses + bracket load path). Revisit with real-snow plate data.

## Belly clearance vs sinkage, L2 sweep (snow stance, walk load)

Ankle pivot 17 mm above the sole. Stance: pivot at 0.92·(L1+L2) below the hip. Belly = 40 mm below the hip axis (ASSUMED). Target: sinkage ≤ 25 % of belly clearance.

| L2 mm | hip height mm | belly clearance mm | 25 % mm | walk sink P4 / P5 mm | pass | knee q2° | belt N (walk) | hip / knee motor Nm |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 130 | 256 | 216 | 54 | 34 / 52 | PASS | 46 | 54 | 0.93 / 0.34 |
| 145 | 270 | 230 | 58 | 34 / 52 | PASS | 46 | 58 | 0.94 / 0.37 |
| 160 | 284 | 244 | 61 | 34 / 52 | PASS | 46 | 62 | 0.95 / 0.39 |

L2 = 130 mm kept: it already passes the clearance target in P4/P5 with the taller stance, keeps L1 = L2 (no unreachable hole), and a longer shank raises distal mass and knee torque in the fold. The L2 lever is available (one parameter) if real snow is softer than P5.

## Traction (A c + W tan φ) vs need (30 % of vertical)

| foot | case | poorly bonded N | well bonded N | needed N | poorly-bonded verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| snowshoe (chosen) | walk (3 down) | 6.9 | 52.1 | 4.4 | PASS |
| snowshoe (chosen) | trot (2 down) | 8.1 | 55.2 | 6.6 | PASS |
| ball R10 | walk (3 down) | 2.5 | 8.1 | 4.4 | SHORT |
| ball R10 | trot (2 down) | 3.7 | 11.3 | 6.6 | SHORT |

Lugs make the shear surface snow-on-snow below the sole, so A is the full planform. On lake/sea ice traction comes from the 4 steel spikes (3 mm proud), not from this model.

## Crust and snow load

- Punch-through resistance scales with perimeter × crust thickness: snowshoe perimeter 325 mm vs ball contact ≈ 63 mm → ≈ 5× the crust load before breaking through (qualitative; test it).
- Snow on the deck: 10 mm of 300 kg/m³ snow on 76 cm² = 23 g (P7) — the top face is flat (it is the print bed face); shake-off relies on the swing and the toe-up tilt.

Required clearance 0.5 mm. Moving parts = STL point clouds (2 mm edge sampling, ≤ 40k points per part); module parts = exact envelopes; thigh body = stadium outline × its z range. The knee-stop sleeves are meant to touch the thigh at 13° / 152° (outside the 15–150° firmware range).

Ankle angles tested: -10.6°, 18.5°, 47.5° (toe-up stop, neutral, toe-down stop).

- Knee sweep, q1 = 0, α = -10.6°: clear 15–137° -> PASS
- Knee sweep, q1 = 0, α = 18.5°: clear 15–137° -> PASS
- Knee sweep, q1 = 0, α = 47.5°: clear 15–137° -> PASS

| knee stop posts at the belt limit | M5 | 1 | knee driven into a stop at 2.29 Nm | 0 | 67 | 2000 | 29.8 | yes | control-failure case |
| ball foot lap → shank (FOOT = 'ball') | M3 | 2 | fall | 0 | 69 | 800 | 11.6 | yes | lap joint in shear |

## Geometry rules (brief 6.4)

- hole Ø as modelled: M3 4.1 mm, M5 6.5 mm (datasheet + 0.1 mm print compensation; coupon holes at ±0.1 to calibrate)
- depth ≥ insert length + 2 pitches: M3 6.7 mm, M5 11.1 mm (the two M5 knee-stop inserts sit in through-holes of the 10 mm shank)
- boss radius = hole radius + one insert OD: M3 r 5.05 (wall 3.00 mm ≥ 3), M5 r 7.00 (wall 3.75 mm)
- every insert hole axis is parallel to its part's print-bed normal (vertical when printed): thigh outer (z, bed +z), inboard plate (z, bed −z), spine (z, bed −z), foot (y, bed +y), outer cheek (z, bed −z), shank (z, bed −z)

**All joints SF ≥ 3: YES**

Not inserts (brief 6.1 exceptions): M2.5 screws into the motors' own threads (hip, knee, ab/ad flanges and back faces; the C-frame tab is clamped by the 5 knee-motor back screws), the torque-carrying hex pockets (knee M5 head and nylock, hip-shaft M5 head), the idler bolt (M3 + nut: it slides in a slot).



===== analysis/skeleton_check.py  (exit 1, 2 s)
# Strength, stiffness and mass — snow leg (analysis/skeleton_check.py)

Allowable in-plane stress 12.5 MPa (25 MPa / SF 2); E = 2300 MPa; robot 4.5 kg; fall = 3 W = 132 N on one foot + 30 % lateral.

## Closed shank: option (a) one closed part vs (b) clamshell

| option | mass g | I in-plane mm⁴ | I out-of-plane mm⁴ | seams into the shank | chosen |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (a) one part, 3 perimeters + 15 % gyroid | 19.0 (slicer) | 4831 | 953 | none | **yes** |
| (b) clamshell, 1.2 mm skins + ribs, 4 × M3 inserts | ≈ 21.1 (estimate) | 4669 | 1195 | one full-length seam | no |

(a) is about the same mass, stiffer out of plane (its skins sit at the full 10 mm thickness), has no seam for snow to wick into and needs no inserts. Section 30 mm below the knee, infill ignored (conservative).

## Shank stresses (snow stance: shank 23° from vertical)

| case | section | in-plane MPa | out-of-plane MPa | Kt | combined MPa | allow | ok |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| walk + 10 % lat | 30 mm below knee | 1.44 | 0.77 | 1 | 2.21 | 12.5 | yes |
| walk + 10 % lat | upper stop post (48 mm) | 1.33 | 0.66 | 2 | 3.97 | 12.5 | yes |
| trot peak + 30 % lat | 30 mm below knee | 3.24 | 5.21 | 1 | 8.45 | 12.5 | yes |
| trot peak + 30 % lat | upper stop post (48 mm) | 3.00 | 4.43 | 2 | 14.84 | 12.5 | **NO** |
| fall + 30 % lat | 30 mm below knee | 12.98 | 20.84 | 1 | 33.82 | 25.0 | **NO** |
| fall + 30 % lat | upper stop post (48 mm) | 11.99 | 17.70 | 2 | 59.38 | 25.0 | **NO** |
| knee peak (belt 120 N → 2.29 Nm) | 30 mm below knee | 5.73 | – | 1 | 5.73 | 12.5 | yes |

Fall cases are checked against the 25 MPa strength (SF 1 for an accident case); service cases against 12.5 MPa.

## Thigh (sealed box, 3 mm walls, no holes): hip-motor peak 4.1 Nm at the root → 1.94 MPa (Kt 2) vs 12.5 -> PASS

## Snowshoe deck under 2.89 kPa (trot), E = 1955 MPa

- heel cantilever (51 mm from the pad, deck + 2 rims): tip 0.23 mm, σ 5.00 MPa
- toe cantilever (25 mm): tip 0.01 mm, σ 0.96 MPa
- side strip (pad edge → rim, 23 mm, deck + lug T-section per 15 mm): 0.007 mm
- worst rim deflection 0.23 mm (target < 2 mm) -> PASS

## Ankle (fall onto the heel tip, toe-down stop engaged)

- moment about the pivot 9.7 Nm → stop force 487 N at r 20 mm
- M5 pin, double shear on the Ø4.0 core: 6 MPa (steel 8.8: ~380 MPa shear) -> PASS
- cheek bearing at the pin (Ø5 × 4.0 mm, per cheek): 3.5 MPa vs 25 -> PASS
- cheek bearing at the stop bolt (Ø3 × 6.7 mm boss, per cheek): 12.1 MPa vs 25 -> PASS
- Ø5 sleeve on the shank edge (10 mm): 9.7 MPa vs 25 -> PASS
- centring springs (2 × 0.1 N/mm, preload 2.0 N): ≈ 0.89 N·mm/° about the pivot; the foot's own weight torque is ≈ 4.7 N·mm, so the springs hold the swing pitch within ≈ 5° of neutral (18.5°)

## Knee stop posts: fall onto a crouched leg at the upper stop → 333 N on the post; M5 (core Ø4.0) bending at 4 mm: 212 MPa vs 640 MPa yield (8.8) → SF 3.0

## Deflection at the ankle pivot, 14.7 N walk load + 10 % lateral (snow stance)
- thigh 0.009 mm, shank in-plane 0.380 mm, shank out-of-plane 0.492 mm → 0.88 mm (target < 1 mm) -> PASS; gearbox backlash adds ≈ 1.4 mm of free play
